explication:
Overview

Pylint is a Python static analyzer. It inspects source without executing it, infers values through the external astroid representation, reports errors and style/code-smell findings, and supports configurable and third-party checks. The repository is primarily a command-line application with extensible Python APIs.

Core components

- CLI and package entry points — pylint/__main__.py
Exposes module execution for command-line use; pylint/__init__.py is the package-level entry surface. - Lint orchestration — pylint/lint
Owns the linter runtime, input/module expansion, parallel execution, caching, message-state handling, run control, and report generation coordination. - Configuration — pylint/config
Defines arguments, configuration-file parsing and discovery, initialization, help formatting, callbacks, and configuration-related errors. User configuration is an external input rather than repository-owned persistent data. - Built-in analysis rules — pylint/checkers
Contains checkers for imports, classes, variables, types, formatting, logging, strings, exceptions, naming, refactoring, version compatibility, and other Python constructs. These are the main rule implementations. - Messages and rule metadata — pylint/message
Defines message objects, message definitions, identifiers, deleted-message tracking, and the message-definition store used to classify and control findings. - Output reporters — pylint/reporters
Provides reporter abstractions and text, JSON, progress, collecting, multi-reporter, and structured-report output implementations. - Shared analysis utilities — pylint/utils
Provides AST walking, file state, pragma parsing, statistics, documentation helpers, and general utilities used by the analyzer. The inferred AST/value model itself is supplied by external astroid.

Relationships

The CLI exposes the linting runtime in pylint/lint. Configuration supplies runtime options and message/checker selection to that runtime. The linter analyzes caller-selected Python files or modules using the external AST/inference layer, while built-in checkers inspect the resulting representation and emit repository-defined messages. Message state and statistics are consumed by reporters to produce the selected output format. Checkers, message definitions, reporters, and configuration form extension boundaries rather than independent sequential applications.

External interfaces and extension points

The primary interface is command-line invocation, with source paths, options, configuration files, and output formats as inputs. Editor/IDE integrations can invoke the same tool. Applications may provide plugins and custom checkers; the documentation identifies plugin loading and custom-checker APIs under doc/development_guide/how_tos. Third-party libraries may require such plugins because standard-library support is built in but external-library support is not universal.

Alternative tools

pylint/pyreverse is a separate diagram-generation tool with its own main, inspection, diagram, printer, and writer areas. Duplicate-code functionality is represented by pylint/checkers/symilar.py and is also documented as the standalone symilar tool. These are optional alternatives to the main linting path, not additional pipeline stages.
